sentences.en: All of these decisions were, you know, quite liberal and quite progressive and really advance a liberal view of American society.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有这些决定都是相当自由的，相当进步的，并且真正推进了美国社会的自由主义观点。

sentences.en: Jason Zengerli reported this story for The Times Magazine.

sentences.en: So while liberals are obviously cheered by this, you know, it starts to dawn on conservatives that the courts are behaving in ways that are hostile to their own interests.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然自由派显然为此感到欢欣鼓舞，但保守派开始意识到，法院的表现方式与他们自身的利益相悖。

sentences.en: And in the minds of these conservatives who object to these landmark cases, what was behind these liberal rulings?
sentences.zh: 在这些反对这些具有里程碑意义的案件的保守派心目中，这些自由派裁决背后的原因是什么？

sentences.en: There were two things.
sentences.zh: 有两件事。

sentences.en: One, there was just the culture of the legal profession, which beginning in law schools, they felt tended to have a liberal bias.
sentences.zh: 第一，这只是法律界的文化，从法学院开始，他们觉得法律界往往有自由派偏见。

sentences.en: So just by its very nature, you were going to have these law schools produce more liberal lawyers.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于其本质，这些法学院将会培养出更多自由派律师。

sentences.en: And the second thing they believed was that Republican politicians, Republican presidents weren't necessarily thinking about conservatism when they pick Supreme Court justices.
sentences.zh: 他们相信的第二件事是，共和党政客、共和党总统在挑选最高法院大法官时，不一定是在考虑保守主义。

sentences.en: They were looking for people who had experience and integrity, but they weren't necessarily thinking about their judicial philosophies.
sentences.zh: 他们寻找的是有经验、有诚信的人，但不一定是在考虑他们的司法哲学。

sentences.en: So they were appointing judges and justices who weren't themselves necessarily that conservative.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们任命的法官和大法官本身不一定那么保守。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So conservatives feel in this period that the entire pipeline, the kind of entire legal system that puts people into judgeships, including the Supreme Court,
sentences.zh: 因此，保守派在此期间感到，整个输送链——即把人送上法官职位（包括最高法院）的整个法律体系，

sentences.en: was doing a pretty bad job of representing their viewpoints and cultivating them.
sentences.zh: 在代表他们的观点和培养他们方面做得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And pipeline's a great word.
sentences.zh: 输送链这个词用得真好。

sentences.en: There was no mechanism for conservatives to climb in that ladder necessarily.
sentences.zh: 保守派没有必然的机制可以爬上那个阶梯。

sentences.en: And then the nation elected a new president tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚国家选出了一位新总统。

sentences.en: Ronald Reagan's lead over President Carter is threatening to become a landslide victory.
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·里根对卡特总统的领先优势正威胁着要变成压倒性的胜利。

sentences.en: Reagan is elected in 1980 and Reagan represents a real sea change for the Republican Party in a number of ways.
sentences.zh: 里根在 1980 年当选，里根在许多方面代表了共和党的真正巨变。

sentences.en: I mean, he's you know, he's the leader of a conservative movement.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，他是保守派运动的领袖。

sentences.en: But that that movement now extends to the courts, the judiciary.
sentences.zh: 但这场运动现在延伸到了法院，延伸到了司法系统。

sentences.en: A lot of conservatives who were angry about the Supreme Court decisions in the 50s, 60s and 70s.
sentences.zh: 许多对 50 年代、60 年代和 70 年代最高法院判决感到愤怒的保守派。

sentences.en: You know, in Reagan, they had a real vehicle and a champion for imposing an ideological view on these judicial appointments.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在里根身上，他们拥有一个真正的工具和拥护者，可以将意识形态观点强加于这些司法任命。

sentences.en: The courts were no longer walled off from these other political considerations.
sentences.zh: 法院不再与这些其他政治考虑隔绝。

sentences.en: But it's another thing to actually have enough of these, you know, conservatively minded judges to actually pick and put on the bench.
sentences.zh: 但要真正拥有足够多这些具有保守思想的法官来挑选并送上法官席，则是另一回事。

sentences.en: And I think conservatives recognized that they needed to start laying the groundwork to actually create these kind of judges.
sentences.zh: 我认为保守派认识到，他们需要开始为实际创建这类法官奠定基础。

sentences.en: If elite law schools were hubs of liberalism,
sentences.zh: 如果精英法学院是自由主义的中心，

sentences.en: they weren't going to produce the kind of lawyers that conservatives would need to stock the bench and actually serve as a counterweight to these liberal judges who had made all of these rulings.
sentences.zh: 它们将无法培养出保守派填补法官席位并真正充当对抗这些做出所有这些裁决的自由派法官的制衡力量所需的律师。

sentences.en: So what do they do to try to create that counterweight?
sentences.zh: 那么他们做了什么来试图创造这种制衡力量呢？

sentences.en: In 1982, you have a group of somewhat disaffected conservative law students at Yale and at Chicago who are feeling beleaguered and out of place and, you know,
sentences.zh: 1982年，在耶鲁大学和芝加哥大学有一群稍微心怀不满的保守派法学院学生，他们感到四面楚歌、格格不入，并且，你知道，

sentences.en: surrounded by liberals everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都被自由派包围。

sentences.en: And they, on their own, establish an organization that they call the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 他们靠自己的力量建立了一个组织，他们称之为联邦党人协会。

sentences.en: Hello, I'm Janice Calabresi, the president of the University of Chicago Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是珍妮丝·卡拉布雷西，芝加哥大学联邦党人协会的主席。

sentences.en: Which will be a home for them.
sentences.zh: 这将是他们的家。

sentences.en: Before I begin, I've had a suggestion that all of you should put the city you're from on your name tags so everybody can get better acquainted.
sentences.zh: 在我开始之前，有人建议你们所有人都应该把你们来自的城市写在名牌上，以便每个人都能更好地了解彼此。

sentences.en: Originally, they just viewed it in some ways as a safe space, just somewhere where they could go to find like-minded people.
sentences.zh: 最初，他们在某些方面只将其视为一个安全空间，一个可以去寻找志同道合的人的地方。

sentences.en: Thank you all for coming.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家的光临。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: I see a lot of new faces in here, a lot of new faces in the hallway coming to a Federalist Society event.
sentences.zh: 我在这里看到了很多新面孔，走廊里也有很多来参加联邦党人协会活动的新面孔。

sentences.en: But pretty soon, the group starts spreading to other campuses.
sentences.zh: 但不久之后，该组织开始向其他校园蔓延。

sentences.en: Hello, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: My name is Ben Massey, and I'm the president of the University of Virginia chapter of the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 我叫本·梅西，我是弗吉尼亚大学联邦党人协会分会的主席。

sentences.en: And conservative law professors.
sentences.zh: 还有保守派法学教授。

sentences.en: These young Federalists, and they are still most in their 20s, they think of themselves as a new generation of young Turks.
sentences.zh: 这些年轻的联邦党人，他们大多数仍在20岁左右，他们认为自己是新一代的年轻土耳其人。

sentences.en: Begin to recognize it as a possible vehicle for young conservative lawyers to get the kind of career training,
sentences.zh: 开始认识到这是年轻保守派律师获得那种职业培训的可能途径，

sentences.en: kind of professional connections that eventually will allow them to be ready to assume a place on the bench.
sentences.zh: 这种职业人脉最终将使他们能够准备好在法官席上占据一席之地。

sentences.en: And so this group that forms the Federalist Society, what's that a reference to?
sentences.zh: 那么这个组建联邦党人协会的群体，这个名字指代什么？

sentences.en: It's a reference to the Federalist Papers, which were a series of essays written by some of the framers of the Constitution
sentences.zh: 它指的是《联邦党人文集》，这是一系列由宪法制定者撰写的文章，

sentences.en: that laid forth the ground rules that governed the early days of the American Republic.
sentences.zh: 制定了管辖美国共和国早期阶段的基本规则。

sentences.en: The Constitution is a written document whose words were debated at length and carefully chosen,
sentences.zh: 宪法是一份书面文件，其字句经过了长时间的辩论和仔细挑选，

sentences.en: and therefore the Founders' handiwork may be presumed to convey an identifiable meaning.
sentences.zh: 因此可以推定开国元勋的心血传达了可识别的含义。

sentences.en: The Federalist Society people were kind of establishing themselves as the guardians of what this country was supposed to be about.
sentences.zh: 联邦党人协会的人将自己确立为这个国家原本应该代表的事物的守护者。

sentences.en: The Constitution itself, by its own terms, is the supreme law of the land, not the body of constitutional decisions which have grown up around it.
sentences.zh: 宪法本身按其自身的条款是国家的最高法律，而不是围绕它发展起来的宪法判决的主体。

sentences.en: They were going to hearken back to its original days.
sentences.zh: 他们将回到其最初的日子。

sentences.en: The courts are bound by the written commands of the Constitution, no less than the executive, no less than the Congress.
sentences.zh: 法院受宪法书面命令的约束，不亚于行政部门，不亚于国会。

sentences.en: And make sure that what was happening today was following what the Founders intended.
sentences.zh: 并确保今天发生的事情遵循开国元勋的意图。

sentences.en: These assertions about American law have found hospitality at the hearth of the Federalist Society at a time when legal academic establishment had barred its doors.
sentences.zh: 这些关于美国法律的主张在联邦党人协会的壁炉旁找到了热情接待，当时法律学术建立机构已经紧闭了大门。

sentences.en: The conservative critique of the courts was that they were out of step with what they were intended to be,
sentences.zh: 保守派对法院的批评是，它们与原本的意图脱节，

sentences.en: that you had judges kind of imposing their own political and personal opinions on things and not sticking to the letter of the law.
sentences.zh: 你会有法官将他们自己的政治和个人观点强加于事物上，而不坚持法律的字面意思。

sentences.en: And I think that's what the Federalist Society believed they were going to counteract.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是联邦党人协会相信他们将要抵制的东西。

sentences.en: Liberals would say the way the country was in the 1950s, 60s, and 70s, you know, it was very different from the country in the 1770s and 1780s.
sentences.zh: 自由派会说，20世纪50年代、60年代和70年代的国家状况，你知道，与1770年代和1780年代的国家非常不同。

sentences.en: And therefore, it was perfectly acceptable and right for judges to try to take these broad principles and guidelines that were established back then and apply them to today.
sentences.zh: 因此，法官试图采用当时建立的这些广泛的原则和指导方针并将它们应用于今天，是完全可以接受和正确的。

sentences.en: But if you stick to the letter of what they're saying, it's a fool's errand.
sentences.zh: 但如果你坚持他们所说的话的字面意思，那就是愚蠢的差事。

sentences.en: So this is really a debate about whether the law should be allowed to be interpreted given the context and the timing of the country at any given moment versus thinking that the law is immutable,
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是一场辩论，即是否应该允许法律根据国家在任何特定时刻的背景和时机进行解释，还是认为法律是不变的，

sentences.en: immovable, and should remain a constant no matter what's happening.
sentences.zh: 不可动摇的，无论发生什么都应该保持不变。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it sounds like the Federalist Society is focusing on establishing that pipeline of lawyers who will adhere to this judicial philosophy that you just laid out.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来联邦党人协会正专注于建立那个律师输送链，他们将坚持你刚刚阐述的这种司法哲学。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, what is President Reagan doing to support that same kind of vision?
sentences.zh: 与此同时，里根总统在做什么来支持同样的那种愿景？

sentences.en: I'm pleased to announce that upon completion of all the necessary checks by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地宣布，在联邦调查局完成所有必要的检查后。

sentences.en: Well, he gets the opportunity to appoint three conservative justices.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他有机会任命三位保守派大法官。

sentences.en: I will send to the Senate the nomination of Judge Sandra Day O'Connor of Arizona.
sentences.zh: 我将向参议院呈交亚利桑那州法官桑德拉·戴·奥康纳的提名。

sentences.en: He appoints O'Connor.
sentences.zh: 他任命了奥康纳。

sentences.en: I am today announcing my intention to nominate United States Circuit Judge Anthony Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 我今天宣布我打算提名美国巡回法院法官安东尼·肯尼迪。

sentences.en: And Kennedy and Scalia.
sentences.zh: 还有肯尼迪和斯卡利亚。

sentences.en: And he also elevates Rehnquist to chief justice.
sentences.zh: 他还将伦奎斯特提升为首席大法官。

sentences.en: I've had the honor of nominating Justice Rehnquist to be the next chief justice of the United States and Judge Scalia to be the associate justice of the United States Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 我有幸提名伦奎斯特大法官为下一任美国首席大法官，并提名斯卡利亚法官为美国最高法院联席大法官。

sentences.en: So this seems to be going very well, this plan to kind of transform the judiciary, and pretty fast if you're a conservative thinker or a member of the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎进展得很顺利，这种改造司法系统的计划，如果你是一个保守派思想家或联邦党人协会的成员，速度非常快。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, at the same time that Reagan is doing this and conservatives are winning the day, the Bork nomination to the Supreme Court is an inflection point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在里根这样做、保守派获胜的同时，对博克的最高法院提名是一个转折点。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, it's my privilege tonight to welcome a most able proponent of the rule of law and the great constitutionalist of our time, Robert Bork.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，今晚我有幸欢迎一位法治的最能干的倡导者和我们时代伟大的宪政主义者，罗伯特·博克。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think the Bork nomination to the Supreme Court is a real moment.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为对最高法院的博克提名是一个真正的时刻。

sentences.en: My opinion is that there are too many laws in this country and that we are redressing too many petty grievances.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，这个国家有太多的法律，我们正在纠正太多的琐碎冤屈。

sentences.en: Democrats on the Hill recognize the threat that Bork posed.
sentences.zh: 国会山上的民主党人认识到了博克构成的威胁。

sentences.en: Bork sides with the president in opposing legalized abortion and many affirmative action decisions.
sentences.zh: 博克与总统站在同一阵线，反对堕胎合法化以及许多平权行动裁决。

sentences.en: Robert Bork's America is a land in which women would be forced into back alley abortions.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·博克的美国是一个妇女被迫进入小巷堕胎的土地。

sentences.en: In Robert Bork's America, there is no room at the inn for blacks and no place in the Constitution for women.
sentences.zh: 在罗伯特·博克的美国，客栈里没有黑人的容身之所，宪法中也没有妇女的位置。

sentences.en: And in our America, there should be no seat on the Supreme Court for Robert Bork.
sentences.zh: 在我们的美国，最高法院不应该有罗伯特·博克的席位。

sentences.en: And defeated him.
sentences.zh: 并击败了他。

sentences.en: That created a sense among some Republicans that they couldn't get too aggressive.
sentences.zh: 这在一些共和党人中产生了一种感觉，即他们不能太激进。

sentences.en: They needed to be a little bit cagier about what they were trying to do.
sentences.zh: 他们需要对他们试图做的事情更加谨慎一点。

sentences.en: Because if you nominate someone like Bork, who was so outspoken and just frontal in terms of his judicial views, they weren't going to be able to get confirmed.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你提名像博克这样直言不讳、在司法观点上非常正面的人，他们将无法获得确认。

sentences.en: And how much of a setback was this for Reagan, conservatives, and the Federalist Society?
sentences.zh: 这对里根、保守派和联邦党人协会来说是一个多大的挫折？

sentences.en: In some ways, it was the defining event for the Federalist Society in its young life.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这是联邦党人协会在其年轻生命中具有决定性的事件。

sentences.en: I mean, I think for a lot of conservative lawyers today, they look back on Bork's defeat as a real moment for them when they realized what they were going to be up againSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为对于今天许多保守派律师来说，他们回顾博克的失败，认为这是他们意识到他们将要面对什么的真正时刻。

sentences.en: But then just on a practical level, because they overshot with Bork, they needed to rein things back in.
sentences.zh: 但从实际层面来看，因为他们在博克身上用力过猛，他们需要把事情收回来。

sentences.en: And so ultimately, Reagan nominates Anthony Kennedy to the seat that Bork would have occupied.
sentences.zh: 因此，最终里根提名安东尼·肯尼迪担任博克本应占据的席位。

sentences.en: And then George H.W.
sentences.zh: 然后老乔治·H·W

sentences.en: Bush appoints David Souter to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 布什任命大卫·苏特进入最高法院。

sentences.en: You know, Reagan and Bush thought that Souter and Kennedy were going to be quite conservative, but there wasn't a lot of evidence for it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，里根和布什认为苏特和肯尼迪会相当保守，但没有太多证据证明这一点。

sentences.en: And as it turned out, they weren't that conservative.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他们并没有那么保守。

sentences.en: They weren't nearly as conservative as, you know, I think that people hoped they would be.
sentences.zh: 他们远没有人们希望的那样保守。

sentences.en: The biggest consequence is Planned Parenthood versus Casey.
sentences.zh: 最大的后果是计划生育诉凯西案。

sentences.en: It's really disturbing that we have to come out here and march for something which is so fundamental as a woman's right to choose.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不出来游行支持如此基础的东西，即女性的选择权，这真的很令人不安。

sentences.en: And so in 1992, you get this case that is the vehicle to overturn Roe.
sentences.zh: 因此，在 1992 年，你得到了这个作为推翻罗诉韦德案工具的案件。

sentences.en: And you have a Supreme Court that has now been stocked with justices who've been appointed by Republican presidents who are considering ideology, considering judicial philosophy.
sentences.zh: 你有一个最高法院，现在里面充斥着由考虑意识形态、考虑司法哲学的共和党总统任命的大法官。

sentences.en: This is what everything has been leading up to.
sentences.zh: 这就是一切一直在引导的方向。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: By a vote of 7 to 2, the court agreed to uphold three of four restrictions on abortions in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 以 7 比 2 的投票结果，法院同意维持宾夕法尼亚州对堕胎的四项限制中的三项。

sentences.en: The court whiffs.
sentences.zh: 法院错失了良机。

sentences.en: Justices Sandra Day O'Connor, David Souter, and Anthony Kennedy wrote,
sentences.zh: 大法官桑德拉·戴·奥康纳、大卫·苏特和安东尼·肯尼迪写道，

sentences.en: The blood of 30 million children is already crying out to Almighty God for vengeance.
sentences.zh: 三千万儿童的鲜血已经在向全能的上帝呼求复仇。

sentences.en: And today, three Reagan-Bush appointees stabbed the pro-life movement in the back and affirmed the bloodshed.
sentences.zh: 而今天，三名里根和布什任命的法官在背后捅了反堕胎运动一刀，并且肯定了这场流血事件。

sentences.en: It whiffs because of these three judges who were appointed by Reagan and Bush who can't pull the trigger.
sentences.zh: 这完全是因为这三位由里根和小布什任命、却下不了决心的法官。

sentences.en: They can't actually follow through and overturn Roe.
sentences.zh: 他们根本无法坚持到底并推翻罗诉韦德案。

sentences.en: And I think that conservative legal activists viewed this as kind of a failure of nerve, that they had not put people on the bench who could actually carry out the mission.
sentences.zh: 我认为保守派法律活动人士认为这是一种勇气上的失败，他们没有把真正能执行这一使命的人送上法官席。

sentences.en: So what conclusion do conservatives draw from this experience about what they need to do next?
sentences.zh: 那么，保守派从这次经历中得出了什么结论，认为接下来他们需要做什么？

sentences.en: There are two conclusions.
sentences.zh: 有两个结论。

sentences.en: One, they need to just start vetting judicial candidates better.
sentences.zh: 第一，他们需要从一开始就更好地审查司法候选人。

sentences.en: And then at the more sort of ground level, they want to redouble their efforts to produce legal minds that ultimately can get on the bench and carry out the mission.
sentences.zh: 然后，在更基础的层面上，他们希望加倍努力培养法律人才，最终让他们进入法庭并完成使命。

sentences.en: And you see that at the law schools, you know, with the Federal Society, which is now maybe 10 years old
sentences.zh: 你可以在法学院看到这一点，你知道的，比如联邦党人协会，现在可能已经有10年历史了。

sentences.en: and has really kind of established itself and has created a network not just in these law schools,
sentences.zh: 它确实确立了自己的地位，并且不仅在这些法学院建立了一个网络，

sentences.en: but, you know, post law school, there are now enough conservative judges on the bench that
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，在法学院毕业后，法官席上现在有了足够多的保守派法官，以至于

sentences.en: if you're a Federal Society, you know, law student, you can then get a clerkship with one of these judges.
sentences.zh: 如果你是联邦党人协会的法学院学生，你就可以在这些法官手下获得书记员职位。

sentences.en: And that's going to lead to a clerkship on the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这将通往最高法院书记员的职位。

sentences.en: And, you know, after you clerk on the Supreme Court, you go to a law firm where there are other
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，在最高法院担任书记员之后，你会去一家律师事务所，那里有其他

sentences.en: Federal Society members, other conservatives, and they groom you.
sentences.zh: 联邦党人协会的成员，其他保守派，他们会培养你。

sentences.en: And you're just kind of carried along at each step of your career by this network that's been built for you.
sentences.zh: 在你职业生涯的每一步，你都会被这个为你建立的网络顺理成章地向前推进。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's a delight to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: And I appreciate very much the invitation by the Federal Society to come and visit with you.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢联邦党人协会邀请我来和大家交流。

sentences.en: You know, by the late 90s, it's gone way beyond just law school campuses.
sentences.zh: 你知道，到90年代末，它已经远远超出了法学院校园的范畴。

sentences.en: It's sort of permeated every level of Republican politics.
sentences.zh: 它几乎渗透到了共和党政治的各个层面。

sentences.en: Good afternoon.
sentences.zh: 大家下午好。

sentences.en: I'm Senator Orrin Hatch, and I'm very happy to be with you this afternoon.
sentences.zh: 我是参议员奥林·哈奇，非常高兴今天下午能与大家在一起。

sentences.en: They're everywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们无处不在。

sentences.en: And it has become kind of the legal arm of the Republican Party in some ways, the judicial arm.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，它已经成为共和党事实上的法律部门，甚至是司法部门。

sentences.en: I'm honored to be with you.
sentences.zh: 我很荣幸能与大家在一起。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I appreciate being with an organization that understands the value of free speech.
sentences.zh: 我很庆幸能加入这样一个理解言论自由价值的组织。

sentences.en: So much so that Gene asked if I'd give one.
sentences.zh: 以至于吉恩问我是否愿意发表一个。

sentences.en: So if you're a Republican, you are subscribing to the views of the Federalist Society when it comes to judicial philosophy and who should be in the courts.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是共和党人，当谈到司法哲学以及谁应该进入法院时，你就是在认同联邦党人协会的观点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The Federalist Society is now big enough that you have to.
sentences.zh: 联邦党人协会现在规模已经大到你不得不这样做。

sentences.en: You have to abide by its views and wishes, and that's something that George W.
sentences.zh: 你必须遵守它的观点和意愿，小布什对此深有体会，

sentences.en: Bush learns the hard way.
sentences.zh: 这是一个惨痛的教训。

sentences.en: A justice must be a person of accomplishment and sound legal judgment.
sentences.zh: 法官必须是有成就且具有良好法律判断力的人。

sentences.en: He has an open Supreme Court seat.
sentences.zh: 他有一个空缺的最高法院席位。

sentences.en: A justice must strictly apply to the Constitution and laws of the United States and not legislate from the bench.
sentences.zh: 大法官必须严格适用美国宪法和法律，而不是在法官席上进行立法。

sentences.en: And he decides to nominate Harriet Myers to fill it.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定提名哈丽特·迈尔斯来填补空缺。

sentences.en: I've known Harriet for more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 我认识哈丽特已经十多年了。

sentences.en: I know her heart.
sentences.zh: 我知道她的内心。

sentences.en: I know her character.
sentences.zh: 我知道她的品格。

sentences.en: But she's someone who the Federalist Society knows nothing about.
sentences.zh: 但她却是联邦党人协会一无所知的人。

sentences.en: As White House counsel, I have enjoyed the opportunity to work with the members of the Congress.
sentences.zh: 作为白宫法律顾问，我很荣幸能有机会与国会议员们共事。

sentences.en: You know, she didn't go to one of these elite law schools.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她没有去过这些精英法学院中的任何一所。

sentences.en: She didn't attend Federalist Society meetings.
sentences.zh: 她没有参加过联邦党人协会的会议。

sentences.en: She didn't really subscribe to their judicial philosophy or their judicial project.
sentences.zh: 她并不真正赞同他们的司法哲学或司法蓝图。

sentences.en: And now I look forward to the next step in the process that has begun this morning.
sentences.zh: 现在我期待着今天上午开始的程序的下一个阶段。

sentences.en: She's not one of them at all.
sentences.zh: 她根本不是他们自己人。

sentences.en: And they make their objections known.
sentences.zh: 他们公开表达了反对意见。

sentences.en: And by that point, they're powerful enough that their objections resonate on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 到那时，他们已经足够强大，以至于他们的反对声音在国会山产生了共鸣。

sentences.en: You must be kidding.
sentences.zh: 你在开玩笑吧。

sentences.en: This cannot be happening.
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能发生。

sentences.en: And Republican senators start to signal that they're not going to vote to confirm her.
sentences.zh: 共和党参议员开始发出信号，表示他们不会投票确认她的提名。

sentences.en: We begin this evening with Harriet Myers.
sentences.zh: 今晚我们从哈丽特·迈尔斯开始。

sentences.en: Earlier today, she withdrew her nomination for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天早些时候，她撤回了对美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 最高法院大法官的提名。

sentences.en: And Myers has to withdraw her nomination.
sentences.zh: 迈尔斯不得不撤回她的提名。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's quite telling that the person Bush nominated in Myers' stead...
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，布什提名的接替迈尔斯的人选非常说明问题……

sentences.en: I am now, and for more than 20 years, have been a member of the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 我目前是，而且二十多年来一直都是联邦党人协会的成员。

sentences.en: With Samuel Alito, who was a Federalist Society darling.
sentences.zh: 塞缪尔·阿利托则是联邦党人协会的宠儿。

sentences.en: And I would add even a card-carrying member of the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 我甚至要补充说，他是联邦党人协会的持证会员。

sentences.en: Except for the fact that I left my membership cards back in my desk in Newark.
sentences.zh: 除了我把会员卡落在了纽瓦克的办公桌里这一事实之外。

sentences.en: I think that was a real moment where the Federalist Society kind of showed that they have to be listened to.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个真正的时刻，联邦党人协会展现出他们是不容忽视的。

sentences.en: So this feels pretty remarkable that in the span of just about 20 years, this organization that had started by opening up chapters on college campuses
sentences.zh: 因此，感觉非常了不起的是，在短短20年左右的时间里，这个最初通过在大学校园里设立分会的组织，

sentences.en: now has enough power to put its foot down and tell the president of the United States no for something as big and important as a Supreme Court seat.
sentences.zh: 现在已经拥有足够的权力来表明立场，并对美国总统说“不”，拒绝涉及像最高法院席位这样重大而重要的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We thought we were just planting a wildflower among the weeds of academic liberalism, and it turned out to be an oak.
sentences.zh: 我们以为自己只是在学术自由主义的杂草中种植了一朵野花，结果它长成了一棵橡树。

sentences.en: And so, you know, by 2007, when they have their 25th anniversary gala in Washington, three sitting Supreme Court justices show up for that and pay homage and pay tribute.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，到了2007年，当他们在华盛顿举办25周年庆典时，三位在任的最高法院大法官出席了晚会并表达了敬意。

sentences.en: If the Federalist Society continues to grow, my concern is that there will not be any location in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 如果联邦党人协会继续发展壮大，我担心华盛顿特区将再也没有任何场地

sentences.en: that will be big enough to hold the event.
sentences.zh: 能够大到容纳这场活动。

sentences.en: Maybe FedEx will be held.
sentences.zh: 也许会租用联邦快递球场。

sentences.en: Remember, it's held.
sentences.zh: 记住，是要举办的。

sentences.en: I hope to be there, and I know that I will see Justice Thomas and Justice Scalia there, and I hope I will see all of you there.
sentences.zh: 我希望能在那里，我也知道我会看到托马斯大法官和斯卡利亚大法官在那里，我希望能在那里见到你们所有人。

sentences.en: So congratulations to the Federalist Society and keep up the good work.
sentences.zh: 所以祝贺联邦党人协会，再接再厉。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 纽约时报应用?

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So with all of this in mind, how does Donald Trump fit into the Federalist Society's view of the world?
sentences.zh: 考虑到所有这些，唐纳德·特朗普是如何契合联邦党人协会的世界观的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I mean, you know, while the Federalist Society is establishing itself and becoming this, you know,
sentences.zh: 对，所以我的意思是，你知道的，正当联邦党人协会确立自己的地位并成为

sentences.en: 800-pound gorilla in Republican politics, Donald Trump misses all that.
sentences.zh: 共和党政治中不可忽视的庞然大物时，唐纳德·特朗普却错过了这一切。

sentences.en: You know, the Federalist Society is not involved in landlord-tenant disputes in New York City.
sentences.zh: 你知道，联邦党人协会并不参与纽约市的房东与房客纠纷。

sentences.en: Like, they don't have a view on that.
sentences.zh: 比如说，他们对此没有看法。

sentences.en: And so it's a good bet he doesn't know what the Federalist Society is when he begins his campaign.
sentences.zh: 因此，可以肯定的是，当他开始竞选时，他并不知道什么是联邦党人协会。

sentences.en: And the Federalist Society certainly doesn't know Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 而联邦党人协会显然也不知道唐纳德·特朗普是谁。

sentences.en: A Trump advisor actually tried to broker a meeting.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的一位顾问实际上曾试图安排一次会面。

sentences.en: If a justice of the Supreme Court cannot be counted on to show complete fidelity to the Constitution, then how can we expect that of anyone?
sentences.zh: 如果最高法院的大法官都不能指望对宪法表现出完全的忠诚，那么我们怎么能对其他人有这种期望呢？

sentences.en: Between Leonard Leo, who was the executive vice president of the Federalist Society, he's kind of the person at the center of the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 在伦纳德·利奥之间，他是联邦党人协会的执行副总裁，他可以说是联邦党人协会的核心人物。

sentences.en: It has never been and never will be too much to ask the justices of our highest court act in honorable adherence to the supreme law of the land.
sentences.zh: 要求我们最高法院的大法官以光荣的态度恪守国家的最高法律，这过去从不过分，将来也永不过分。

sentences.en: And a Trump advisor named Sam Nunberg, he told me the story about how he went up to Leo and said,
sentences.zh: 特朗普的一位名叫萨姆·南伯格的顾问，他跟我讲了一个故事，说他走到利奥面前说，

sentences.en: you know, you're not going to believe, you know, Mr. Trump's changed all of his positions on the things you care about.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你不会相信的，你知道，特朗普先生已经改变了他对你所关心的事情的所有立场。

sentences.en: He's now on your side and you're not going to believe how good he's going to be for you.
sentences.zh: 他现在站在你这边，你根本不会相信他对你有多好。

sentences.en: And Nunberg said that, you know, Leo just kind of nodded his head very politely and listened to him.
sentences.zh: 南伯格说，你知道的，利奥只是非常礼貌地点了点头，听着他说话。

sentences.en: He called it a Washington listen.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“华盛顿式的倾听”。

sentences.en: And the meeting never happened.
sentences.zh: 这次会面最终没有发生。

sentences.en: But...
sentences.zh: 但是……

sentences.en: He has been the GOP frontrunner for months now.
sentences.zh: 几个月来他一直是共和党初选的领跑者。

sentences.en: Even Donald Trump's controversial comments don't seem to hurt his poll numbers too much.
sentences.zh: 即使是唐纳德·特朗普那些充满争议的言论似乎也没有对他的民调数字造成太大影响。

sentences.en: By early 2016...
Donald Trump's number is bigger than the number two, three, and four candidates combined.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的支持率超过了第二、三、四名候选人的总和。

sentences.en: Leonard Leo's thoughts about Donald Trump's political aspirations have evolved.
sentences.zh: 伦纳德·利奥对唐纳德·特朗普政治抱负的想法已经发生了演变。

sentences.en: And he realizes that he's not in a position where he can really afford to ignore Trump anymore.
sentences.zh: 他意识到自己已经不再处于能够真正忽视特朗普的境地了。

sentences.en: But I think at another level, it's even more interesting than that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在另一个层面上，它甚至比这更有趣。

sentences.en: All the things that would lead the Federalist Society to kind of turn their nose up at Trump all of a sudden become opportunities.
sentences.zh: 所有那些会让联邦党人协会对特朗普嗤之以鼻的事情突然都变成了机遇。

sentences.en: You know, Trump is so unformed in terms of his judicial philosophy, in terms of his thoughts about judges, just how much he cares about this stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，特朗普在司法哲学方面、在对法官的想法方面、以及他究竟有多关心这些事情上，都显得非常不成熟。

sentences.en: I think Leo recognizes that this is actually an incredible opportunity, that they can get in on the ground floor with Trump and they can take ownership of this issue.
sentences.zh: 我认为利奥意识到这其实是一个绝佳的机会，他们可以与特朗普从底层切入，并接管这个议题。

sentences.en: I mean, they've always had influence with Republican presidents, but Trump offers them something even more than influence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们过去对共和党总统一直有影响力，但特朗普提供给他们的不仅仅是影响力。

sentences.en: It's almost like Trump could be willing to subcontract to them this entire thing.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像特朗普愿意把整件事情外包给他们一样。

sentences.en: Because he's kind of a blank slate when it comes to judicial philosophy.
sentences.zh: 因为在司法哲学方面，他基本上是一张白纸。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I can see why the Federalist Society wouldn't want to work with Trump.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以理解为什么联邦党人协会不想与特朗普合作。

sentences.en: But why would Trump want to work with the Federalist Society?
sentences.zh: 但为什么特朗普会想和联邦党人协会合作呢？

sentences.en: Why would this fiercely independent figure, who is challenging everything about the Republican Party and its orthodoxies as a candidate,
sentences.zh: 为什么这个作为候选人正在挑战共和党及其一切正统观念的极度独立的人物，

sentences.en: want to work with this group that's like an emblem of Republican ideology?
sentences.zh: 会想要与这个象征着共和党意识形态的群体合作？

sentences.en: Because Trump, despite all of his rebelliousness, despite all of his outsider status, there's just the matter of getting votes.
sentences.zh: 因为特朗普，尽管他充满叛逆，尽管他有着局外人的身份，但归根结底还是要争取选票。

sentences.en: And he knows that there's a large group of Republican voters that the thing they care about most is the courts.
sentences.zh: 他知道有一大批共和党选民，他们最关心的事情就是法院。

sentences.en: And he needs to convince those voters that he's going to be reliable.
sentences.zh: 他需要让这些选民确信他是靠得住的。

sentences.en: I'm going to submit a list of justices, potential justices of the United States Supreme Court, that I will appoint from the liSt.
sentences.zh: 我将提交一份大法官候选人名单，即我将从这份名单中任命的美国最高法院潜在法官。

sentences.en: And the best way he can signal to those voters that he will do what they want him to do.
sentences.zh: 而他能向这些选民发出信号表明他会按他们的意愿行事的最好方式，

sentences.en: I'm going to let people know because some people say, oh, maybe I'll appoint a liberal judge.
sentences.zh: 我要让大家知道，因为有些人说，哦，也许我会任命一个自由派法官。

sentences.en: I'm not appointing a liberal judge.
sentences.zh: 我不会任命自由派法官。

sentences.en: Is by getting the seal of approval from the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 就是获得联邦党人协会的盖印批准。

sentences.en: So I went to the Federalist Society, which is sort of the gold standard.
sentences.zh: 所以我去找了联邦党人协会，这可以说是黄金标准。

sentences.en: He needs the Federalist Society's endorsement as much as the Federalist Society needs him.
sentences.zh: 他需要联邦党人协会的背书，正如联邦党人协会需要他一样。

sentences.en: So I went out and I said, you know what I'm going to do?
sentences.zh: 所以我走出去说，你知道我要做什么吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to pick 10 judges or 11 judges and we'll see what happens.
sentences.zh: 我要挑选10名或11名法官，我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: And I picked 11, gotten from the Federalist Society, run through.
sentences.zh: 我挑选了11个人，都是从联邦党人协会挑选的，经过了筛选。

sentences.en: So he goes to Leonard Leo, who does nothing but think about who the right candidates would be for the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所以他找到了伦纳德·利奥，后者整天只考虑谁才是最高法院的合适人选。

sentences.en: And he says, I want you to give me a list of names who I can put on the court.
sentences.zh: 他说，我需要你给我一份名单，我可以把人选安排进法院。

sentences.en: And, you know, Leonard Leo is very happy to oblige.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，伦纳德·利奥非常乐意效劳。

sentences.en: So he essentially does subcontract this out to the Federalist Society, not in any kind of metaphorical way, like literally.
sentences.zh: 所以他本质上确实把这件事外包给了联邦党人协会，不是什么比喻意义上的，而是字面意义上的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: All pretenses have fallen away.
sentences.zh: 所有的伪装都消失了。

sentences.en: I mean, George W.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，小布什

sentences.en: Bush picked Samuel Alito because he knew the Federalist Society liked him.
sentences.zh: 选择塞缪尔·阿利托是因为他知道联邦党人协会喜欢他。

sentences.en: And after the Myers debacle, he needed to make sure he stayed on the good side of the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 在迈尔斯惨败之后，他需要确保自己保持在联邦党人协会的好感名单上。

sentences.en: But he wouldn't necessarily admit to that.
sentences.zh: 但他不会轻易承认这一点。

sentences.en: He wouldn't do it out in the open.
sentences.zh: 他不会公开这样做。

sentences.en: Trump, he doesn't worry about those niceties.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普，他不用担心这些繁文缛节。

sentences.en: He's just, he needs to reassure these people that he's going to pick the right judges.
sentences.zh: 他只是，他需要向这些人保证他会挑选正确的法官。

sentences.en: And the best way to do that is to say,
sentences.zh: 而做到这一点的最好方法就是说，

sentences.en: I'm going to have the Federalist Society pick them for me.
sentences.zh: 我要让联邦党人协会帮我挑选。

sentences.en: So he just goes ahead and says it.
sentences.zh: 所以他直接就这么说了。

sentences.en: Appreciate all of the help in deciding who to pick for the United States Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家在决定由谁出任美国最高法院大法官时提供的所有帮助。

sentences.en: And Leonard, you were fantastic.
sentences.zh: 伦纳德，你太棒了。

sentences.en: All of your work.
sentences.zh: 你所有的工作。

sentences.en: So what is handing this process over to the Federalist Society actually look like?
sentences.zh: 那么，把这个过程交由联邦党人协会来主导，实际情况到底是怎样的呢？

sentences.en: Once Trump is elected.
sentences.zh: 一旦特朗普当选。

sentences.en: So before Trump even takes office, Leo joins the transition team.
sentences.zh: 所以，甚至在特朗普就职之前，利奥就加入了过渡团队。

sentences.en: And together with Don McGahn, who was the Trump campaign lawyer and has now been tapped to be Trump's White House counsel,
sentences.zh: 并且与唐·麦甘——他曾是特朗普竞选团队的律师，现已被挑选为特朗普的白宫法律顾问——

sentences.en: and, you know, who also happens to have been a longtime member of the Federalist Society, he and Leo begin picking people for these vacancies because there's so many of them.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他恰好也是联邦党人协会的长期成员，他和利奥开始为这些空缺职位挑选人选，因为空缺实在太多了。

sentences.en: I mean, when Trump is elected, there are over 100 judicial vacancies.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当特朗普当选时，有超过100个司法空缺职位。

sentences.en: So they start, you know, nominating dozens at a time.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始，你知道的，一次提名几十个人。

sentences.en: The White House announces its, quote, 16th wave of judicial nominees.
sentences.zh: 白宫宣布了其所谓的“第16波”司法提名人选。

sentences.en: You know, when the White House releases the names of these nominations, they refer to them as waves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当白宫公开发布这些提名人选的名字时，他们将其称为“波”。

sentences.en: Part of a tsunami of Trump judicial nominees throughout the United States federal court system.
sentences.zh: 这是席卷全美联邦法院系统的一股特朗普司法提名浪潮的一部分。

sentences.en: They're all the way up, I think, now to the 17th wave.
sentences.zh: 我想，他们现在已经推进到第17波了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And up on the Hill.
sentences.zh: 而在国会山。

sentences.en: And now here are the ones in the bullpen right now waiting for their time for confirmation.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些是目前在候补区等待确认听证会的人。

sentences.en: They're just trying to push these things through as fast as they can.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在尽最大努力尽快把这些事情推过去。

sentences.en: Mitchell Hall's doing the right thing in getting these lifetime appointments on the bench.
sentences.zh: 米切尔·霍尔正在做正确的事情，把这些终身任命的法官席位搞定。

sentences.en: So Trump has gotten 26 appeals court judges confirmed in his first two years, which is unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 因此，特朗普在他头两年里已经有26名上诉法院法官获得确认，这是史无前例的。

sentences.en: Trump is outpacing all of his predecessors.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的发展速度超过了他所有的前任。

sentences.en: And those appellate court judges are inevitably in the pipeline to become Supreme Court justices eventually.
sentences.zh: 而这些上诉法院法官不可避免地会进入成为最高法院大法官的后备通道。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the proving ground.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是试金石。

sentences.en: Neil Gorsuch, who was Trump's first Supreme Court nominee, who's now on the Supreme Court, he came from the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·戈萨奇是特朗普的第一位最高法院提名人，他现在已经在最高法院了，他来自第十巡回上诉法院。

sentences.en: Brett Kavanaugh, who Trump has nominated at the Supreme Court, is waiting to be confirmed.
sentences.zh: 布雷特·卡瓦诺是特朗普提名的最高法院人选，正等待确认。

sentences.en: He came from the D.C.
sentences.zh: 他来自哥伦比亚特区

sentences.en: Circuit Court of Appeals.
sentences.zh: 巡回上诉法院。

sentences.en: And they originated in that Federalist Society pipeline.
sentences.zh: 而他们都源于联邦党人协会的那条人才管道。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Good afternoon.
sentences.zh: 下午好。

sentences.en: I'm Brett Kavanaugh of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我是美国哥伦比亚特区

sentences.en: Court of Appeals for the D.C.
sentences.zh: 巡回上诉法院的

sentences.en: Circuit.
sentences.zh: 布雷特·卡瓦诺。

sentences.en: So take Brett Kavanaugh, whose confirmation hearings start today.
sentences.zh: 所以以布雷特·卡瓦诺为例，他的确认听证会今天开始。

sentences.en: Thank you to the Federalist Society and particularly to Gene Meyer and Leonard Leo for organizing this superb convention.
sentences.zh: 感谢联邦党人协会，特别是吉恩·迈尔和伦纳德·利奥组织了这次精彩的会议。

sentences.en: He's as pure a product of the Federalist Society as exists.
sentences.zh: 他是联邦党人协会最纯粹的产物。

sentences.en: He joins the Federalist Society when he's at Yale Law School.
sentences.zh: 他在耶鲁法学院就读时加入了联邦党人协会。

sentences.en: He ultimately goes to work in George W.
sentences.zh: 他最终进入乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush's White House.
sentences.zh: 布什的白宫工作。

sentences.en: George W.
sentences.zh: 乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush appoints him to the D.C.
sentences.zh: 布什任命他担任哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院法官。

sentences.en: Circuit Court of Appeals.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，他曾担任最高法院安东尼·肯尼迪的助理书记官。

sentences.en: Before that, he clerked for Anthony Kennedy on the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，他是联邦党人协会一直以来试图做的事情的典范。

sentences.en: In some ways, he's the poster child for what the Federalist Society has tried to do.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，他是联邦党人协会一直以来试图做的事情的典范。

sentences.en: So now, with Gorsuch already on the court and Kavanaugh on the verge of being on the court, we have in the Federalist Society this group that's kind of scrappily formed out
sentences.zh: 所以现在，随着戈萨奇已经进入法院，卡瓦诺也即将进入法院，我们拥有了联邦党人协会这个群体，它最初是由反对他们所认为的这个自由派司法系统的群体

sentences.en: of opposition to what they see as this liberal judicial system, now very much on the cusp of taking over the most powerful court in the country and effectively reversing this thing
sentences.zh: 艰难组建而成的，现在他们非常接近接管这个国家最有权力的法院，并实际上扭转了他们

sentences.en: that they were formed to try to challenge.
sentences.zh: 最初为之成立并试图挑战的事物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They've been playing a long game for, you know, three decades, and they're now on the cusp of achieving what they set out to do.
sentences.zh: 他们已经进行了一场漫长的博弈，你知道的，持续了三十年，而他们现在即将实现他们的既定目标。

sentences.en: It's kind of amazing how efficiently this group has done something that's unfathomably ambitious to do in a generation.
sentences.zh: 这个群体能够以如此高的效率完成在一代人看来极其雄心勃勃、不可思议的事情，这真是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a real testament to their vision and then their discipline.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实证明了他们的远见和纪律性。

sentences.en: They haven't taken their eye off the ball.
sentences.zh: 他们没有把视线从目标上移开。

sentences.en: You know, other people weren't paying attention to this, and they were very focused in terms of accomplishing their goals.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，其他人并没有注意到这一点，而他们在实现目标方面非常专注。

sentences.en: Jason, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 杰森，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来节目。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 今天你还需要了解以下内容。

sentences.en: The point I'm going to make is that this is not normal.
sentences.zh: 我要指出的是，这并不正常。

sentences.en: You have a nominee with excellent credentials with his family behind him.
sentences.zh: 你有一个履历优秀、家人在后支持的被提名人。

sentences.en: You have the cameras there.
sentences.zh: 你在那里架设了摄像机。

sentences.en: You have the senators questioning.
sentences.zh: 你让参议员们进行质询。

sentences.en: But this isn't normal.
sentences.zh: 但这并不正常。

sentences.en: It's not normal because we are not able to see 100,000 documents because the administration has said we can't see them.
sentences.zh: 这不正常，因为我们无法看到十万份文件，因为政府表示我们不能看。

sentences.en: The Trump administration is refusing to give the Senate more than 100,000 pages of records from Judge Kavanaugh's time as a lawyer in the administration of George W.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府拒绝向参议院提供超过十万页的记录，这些记录关于卡瓦诺法官在乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush, infuriating
sentences.zh: 布什政府担任律师期间的经历，这激怒了

sentences.en: Democrats.
sentences.zh: 民主党人。

sentences.en: In withholding the documents, the administration is citing executive privilege, arguing that
sentences.zh: 在隐瞒这些文件时，政府援引了行政特权，争辩称

sentences.en: the records contain internal deliberations and candid advice to President Bush and those around him that were never intended to be public.
sentences.zh: 这些记录包含向布什总统及其周围人员提供的内部审议和坦诚建议，这些内容从未打算公之于众。

sentences.en: The White House has already turned over more than 415,000 pages of Kavanaugh's records to the Senate, which are likely to be the basis for senators' questions to Kavanaugh during
sentences.zh: 白宫已经向参议院移交了超过41.5万页的卡瓦诺记录，这些很可能是参议员在确认听证会上对卡瓦诺提问的基础。

sentences.en: his confirmation hearings.
sentences.zh: 这些听证会将于今天上午开始。

sentences.en: Those hearings begin this morning.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时甚至惊心动魄的斗争中。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
